newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed despite key index gains.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed despite key index gains.

* Despite gains in Toronto's key stock index, the broader market ended mixed on Tuesday as losing issues edged out winners 498 to 481. * 93 million shares traded, valued at C$1.7 billion.
Despite gains in Toronto's key stock index, the broader market ended mixed in moderate dealings on Tuesday as weaker commodity prices dragged many issues down.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index climbed 53.25 points to close at 6490.96. Trading totaled 92.8 million shares worth C$1.7 billion.

Toronto rose amid New York's 153-point rebound to 7758 points after Monday's 192-point sell-off. "We weren't down as much as they were yesterday, so we aren't up as much," said Yorkton Securities trader Pier Donnini.
Declining issues edged out advancers 498 to 481, while 312 ended even.
Weak commodity prices such as gold bullion pressured many stocks, analysts said. "Golds are a persistent problem," Donnini said.

Financial issues and other takeover targets grabbed investor attention on Tuesday. "If you look at the rest of the companies, nothing much happened," said Maison Placements Canada trader Rolie Bradley.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes added points, led by banks, transportation and media. Slipping sectors included conglomerates and golds.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Bank of Nova Scotia, the nation's fourth largest, rose 2.25 to a 52-week high of 60.05 after news that it offered to acquire National Trustco Inc in a deal valued at C$1.25 billion.
In another move by a Canadian bank, takeover target London Insurance Group said it was in merger talks with the country's largest bank, Royal Bank of Canada.
London Insurance added 2.80 to 26.30, while Royal Bank edged up 1.15 to a 52-week high of 63.15.
* Shares in Southam Inc closed 1.25 higher at 23.50 after Hollinger Inc's C$23.50 a share bid for Southam's minority shares was rejected late on Monday.
